clue.text: White dwarf found by Galileo initially? Only half of it visible

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the astronomer's name

parts.note: it is slang for sex, rumpy-pumpy, and only half of that rhyming phrase is kept, the front portion

explanation.surface: An astronomy question: did Galileo spot a white dwarf star, only half of it visible?
explanation.walkthrough: 'White dwarf' looks like a star but is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs. 'it' means sex, RUMPY-PUMPY, and 'Only half of' keeps RUMPY; 'visible' just finishes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven dwarfs in Disney's Snow White is the bad-tempered one of that name.

clue.text: Polish composer and Russian writer talked about touring the City

indicators.note: touring means the sounded name goes round the City postcode
talked about means the writer's name is taken as spoken, allowing another spelling

parts.note: Maxim Gorky was a Russian writer
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A Polish composer and a Russian author discussed on a tour of London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district of the City of London, the financial square mile. Henryk Górecki wrote the Symphony of Sorrowful Songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Henryk Górecki was a twentieth-century Polish composer famed for his Third Symphony.

clue.text: Unadulterated state

definitions.meaning: complete, absolute, as in sheer nonsense
to say or declare something out loud

explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or absolute; as a verb it means to speak or declare.

clue.text: Glen Ponder gets aroused by Linda Lovelace?

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the name's letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Glen Ponder is excited by the 1970s adult-film actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Linda Lovelace was the star of the 1972 film Deep Throat; the question mark marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovelace was one of the most famous stars of adult films, an icon of that industry.

clue.text: Is removing Johnson's shilling pieces called for?

parts.note: a bob was slang for the old British shilling coin

indicators.note: called signals that the word for the pieces is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: pieces are bits

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Boris Johnson's shilling coins ought to be taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnson' is slang for a penis, not the politician; Lorena Bobbitt famously cut off her husband's, so to bobbitt is to do that. A bob is an old British shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorena Bobbitt's notorious act gave a verb for severing a man's member, and Johnson is slang for that organ.

clue.text: Maybe Patsy Cline's second whiskey and soda on the rocks

indicators.note: on the rocks means wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reordered
second asks for the second letter of the singer's name

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The country singer Patsy Cline's second drink, a whiskey and soda over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patsy' is not the singer's first name but a fall guy: Lee Harvey Oswald claimed to be a patsy. 'Maybe' marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee Harvey Oswald, accused assassin of JFK, insisted he was just a patsy, a scapegoat.

clue.text: Weary of York? Head down south

indicators.note: in a down clue south is the bottom, so the leading letter goes to the end

parts.note: Ebor, from Latin Eboracum, is the signature of the Archbishop of York, meaning of York

explanation.surface: Someone from York, tired, heads south.
explanation.walkthrough: Ebor is the Latin-derived name used for York, as in the Ebor horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: To weary someone is to tire them with dullness, which is what a tedious talker does.

clue.text: Long-winded story about king and mother discovered

indicators.note: about means the story wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a tale is a story
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, the outer letters stripped away

parts.note: native, as in mother tongue or native tongue, means of one's origin

explanation.surface: A tedious story about a king and his mother being found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means uncovered: the mother word loses its outer letters. 'mother' gives NATIVE as in mother tongue, native tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone garrulous goes on at length, so wordy and chatty are near synonyms.

clue.text: Cash and curry? 29 it is!

definitions.meaning: slang for money, as in short of the readies
to curry a horse is to rub it down with a comb, to rake its coat
the answer at 29 across, Old Nick

explanation.surface: A takeaway question: pay cash for the curry? 29 says yes!
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: slang money, the verb curry (groom a horse with a comb), and Old Scratch, the 29 across answer. 'curry' is not the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch is slang money, a currycomb scrapes a horse's coat, and Old Scratch names Satan.

clue.text: The earth may sometimes discharge water, ultimately in this

definitions.text: The earth may sometimes discharge water, ultimately in this

parts.note: Ge, or Gaea, is the Greek earth goddess, so earth

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the last letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Describing a natural spring where the ground sometimes spouts water.
explanation.walkthrough: GE is a rare name for the earth, from the Greek goddess Gaea. The whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring from which the ground periodically discharges a jet of water.

clue.text: 24 in desert

indicators.note: in, after the cross-reference, means put into the state that phrase names, a plastic or remoulded form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer at 24 across is a two-word phrase whose second word, art, is the material here

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: something to be found inside the answer to 24.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 across is PLASTIC ART: 'plastic' means mouldable, so ART in plastic form is ART reshaped into RAT. The blog reads it the same way: an anagram of ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat is to abandon your side, as a deserter does, so the verb sense of desert matches.

clue.text: Singer concerned with Liberal supporter and Welsh Democrat, always looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the whole chain of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a bra is an undergarment that supports
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A politician's speech linking a Liberal backer and a Welsh Democrat, forever living in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns RELBRAWDEER around; EER is the poetic E'ER, always.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown songbird of reedbeds is a singer in the crossword sense of a bird that sings.

clue.text: Pat's literally gutted with the French intervening without much thought

indicators.note: intervening means the French article comes between letters of the stroking word

parts.note: to pat is to stroke gently, to caress; the 's joins it to the rest
le is French for the

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of the word are removed, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: Pat is literally gutted, with French people getting involved thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties 'literally' of all but its ends, and 'intervening' puts the French article within the word for a stroke; 'Pat's' is the verb, pat as in stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carelessly means acting heedlessly, with little attention or forethought.

clue.text: Island nation finally banned whisky

indicators.note: finally banned says the last letter of the island state is removed

parts.note: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation

explanation.surface: A small island country has at last prohibited whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A single malt is a type of Scotch, so the short name stands for that whisky.

clue.text: Comic Paul Riley entertains college in a funny way

indicators.note: entertains means the rearranged name hosts the college inside it
comic means funny or absurd, so the comedian's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedian named Paul Riley performs at a university, raising some laughs.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny can mean strange or odd, and peculiarly means oddly, in a strange manner.

clue.text: English writer, Sir Hugo, involved originally in play

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of the following word
in play means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer and a knight called Hugo both had a part in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes I from 'involved', and 'in play' rearranges SIRHUGO with it. Kazuo Ishiguro, Japanese-born, is a British novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazuo Ishiguro, Nobel laureate and author of The Remains of the Day, grew up and writes in England.

clue.text: He loves her SS pants and footwear

indicators.note: pants means jumbled up or rubbish, signalling these letters are reordered

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so two loves are two O shapes

explanation.surface: A man adores a woman's Nazi-themed underwear and shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like the underwear but signals an anagram; a love is a zero, O, in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron plate is nailed to a horse's hoof, making it the animal's footwear.

clue.text: "Thing from Another World", screened by school?

indicators.note: screened by means one piece is hidden behind another, so it sits inside

parts.note: a school is a shoal of fish
ET, the extraterrestrial, comes from another world

explanation.surface: The sci-fi film The Thing from Another World being shown at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the 1951 film, but 'Thing' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something means an obsession with it, which is what a fixation or fetish is.

clue.text: Drop of milky liquid for 10?

indicators.note: a drop of a word here is its first letter, the opening drip

parts.note: urine is a bodily liquid

explanation.surface: A doctor's question about a drop of milky fluid given to a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the answer RAT, so the definition means 'relating to rats', the zoological adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological adjective for the mouse and rat family describes anything pertaining to such rodents.

clue.text: You won't be able to see Maria after this time

definitions.text: You won't be able to see Maria after this time

parts.words: You won't be able to see Maria after this time
parts.note: maria are the dark plains, or seas, on the lunar surface, which disappear from view once it sinks below the horizon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Maria' looks like a woman's name but is the plural of mare, the dark seas on the moon's face.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon goes below the horizon its dark seas can no longer be seen, so this is that moment.

clue.text: It's impolitic ignoring Queen — but it's bold

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving the royal abbreviation out of the longer word

parts.note: impolitic means unwise, imprudent
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for Queen

explanation.surface: Bypassing the monarch may be undiplomatic, but it is brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent behaviour is cheeky and brazen, a bold disregard for respect.

clue.text: Patriarch's tessellation

definitions.meaning: belonging to Moses, the biblical patriarch and lawgiver, as in his law
a picture made of small tiles fitted together

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective of Moses describes his law, and the noun is a picture of tiny tiles, tesserae.

clue.text: Pottered about after releasing pressure valve

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are moved around into a new order
after releasing means the pressure letter has been let out of the word

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone potters about after letting the pressure out of a valve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after releasing' drops P from POTTERED, leaving OTTERED, and 'about' rearranges it. A tetrode is an old thermionic valve with four electrodes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermionic valve, or vacuum tube, with four electrodes is named from the Greek for four.

clue.text: Stuff that's retracted fundamental muscles?

parts.note: to glut is to stuff or overfill

indicators.note: retracted means taken back, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Stuff that has shrunk back, the basic muscles?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fundamental' plays on fundament, the buttocks; the gluteus muscles are the ones in the seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The gluteus muscles form the buttocks, the fundament, so they are literally fundamental muscles.

clue.text: I finish off beer in a single continuous action

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: finish off asks for the closing letter of the drink

explanation.surface: A drinker boasts of downing a beer in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the Roman numeral for one, spelt out as ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: In film or cricket slang, a oner is something done in one go, like an unbroken take.

clue.text: At the end I see some overwhelming sculpture?

indicators.note: overwhelming means the portion word engulfs the others, holding them inside

parts.note: some means part, a portion
at the end means last
see is the sound of the letter C

explanation.surface: Someone finally sees a sculpture that overwhelms them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' gives C by sound, the letter's name. The question mark admits sculpture is only one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: The plastic arts are those that shape material, such as modelling or carving, of which sculpture is the chief example.

clue.text: Some yogi masters turned up in China

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upwards
some means just a part of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: Some yoga masters appeared in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate. 'Some' takes OGIMA from the words, and 'turned up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, the same as the Spanish word for a pal.

clue.text: Vice-Admiral at games has to use electronic cigarettes

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Vice-Admiral
PE, physical education, is school games

explanation.surface: A naval officer at a sporting event must use e-cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, school games lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaping is inhaling vapour from an e-cigarette, the modern substitute for smoking.

clue.text: More corny 13, unknown among nouveaux riches

indicators.note: among puts the whisky and the unknown inside the rearranged wealth
nouveaux riches suggests riches made new, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: 13 across is the whisky answer, MALT
Z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A sneer at vulgar new money drinking whisky, with a stranger among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nouveaux' looks like part of the French phrase but signals a rearrangement of 'riches', giving SCHIER; '13' points to the whisky answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is mawkish sentimentality, so something schmaltzier is more sugary and trite, more corny.

clue.text: Language used by Lord Jim occasionally when going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way says the picked letters are read backwards
occasionally means taking only every other letter of the novel's title

explanation.surface: The language Conrad's hero Lord Jim used now and then when going astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' picks O, D, I from LORD JIM; 'going the wrong way' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial international language derived from Esperanto in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Deuce! It's time he was back

indicators.note: back says the word for existed is read in reverse

parts.note: to have lived is to have existed, to have been

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire calls deuce and says it is time the player returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deuce!' is an old exclamation meaning 'the Devil!', not the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: Deuce is an old euphemism for Satan, used in oaths like 'what the deuce'.

clue.text: Power of film that takes place in Ulster

definitions.meaning: the Hollywood star Power, of The Mark of Zorro, had this first name
a county of Northern Ireland, one of Ulster's six

explanation.surface: Something filmed on location in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' is the surname of the actor, not strength; Tyrone is also one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrone Power was a 1930s-50s screen star, and County Tyrone lies in Ulster.
